first_impression.reaction: Googled 'notice of intended marriage' on the train because my fiance's family is in Melbourne and someone said we need 'a NOIM'. The first two sentences tell me what it is, who gets it and the one month to 18 month window, dated this month. That's my answer. I kept going for the overseas bit and the witness rules, then the FAQ, and I'd bookmark it.

journey.quote: As at November 2026, it must reach your celebrant at least one month and no more than 18 months before the day.
journey.reaction: Straight answer with a date on it. That's the 'is this still true?' question handled before I even ask it.

journey.quote: If you plan to marry legally in another country instead, the NOIM does not come into it: you follow that country's rules.
journey.reaction: Useful, tells me quickly whether this is even my problem. It is, we're marrying in Australia.

journey.quote: When the legal route is settled, [Wedded Concierge] can take on the celebration.
journey.reaction: A sales line before the takeaways. It's one sentence so I just thumb past it, but it's a bit early.

journey.quote: Since 12 June 2024 it can be witnessed in person or by audio-visual link, but a couple overseas needs a non-celebrant witness who is also overseas, in person.
journey.reaction: This is the one that matters to me, living in Singapore. Clear enough on one read: no video call for us, find someone here.

journey.quote: Destination couples either marry legally in Australia and celebrate abroad, which needs a NOIM, or marry legally abroad under local rules, often with a Certificate of No Impediment.
journey.reaction: Long for a phone bullet, and 'Certificate of No Impediment' is a new term I don't need yet. Had to reread it.

journey.section: When do you need to lodge your NOIM?
journey.quote: Treat that as a floor, not a target.
journey.reaction: Good practical nudge. Headings under this section match exactly what I'd ask: earliest, latest, missed it.

journey.section: How to fill out the NOIM form step by step
journey.quote: Each of you completes your own details on the form.
journey.reaction: That's the whole of Step 2? The heading promised 'how to fill out', and this step doesn't really tell me anything. Fine, the form is short, but it feels thin.

journey.section: Who can witness a Notice of Intended Marriage?
journey.quote: The authorised witnesses are listed in the "Signatures of parties and witnesses" section of the NOIM.
journey.reaction: Just tell me who can witness it. I'm on a phone; now I have to open a PDF to get the actual answer to the heading's question. The location rules after it are clear though.

journey.section: Lodging a NOIM when you live overseas
journey.quote: Your authorised witness must be outside Australia with you, cannot be a celebrant, and must witness in person, because a NOIM for a couple outside Australia cannot be witnessed online.
journey.reaction: Exactly my situation, in one sentence. Screenshot for my fiance.

journey.section: Can the one-month notice be shortened?
journey.quote: Approval is never automatic, so start with your celebrant and treat a shortening of time as a fallback, not a plan.
journey.reaction: Honest. The grounds list is easy to scan and there's a link to the actual authorities. Proper government links throughout make me trust it.

journey.section: NOIM or marrying abroad: which paperwork applies?
journey.quote: You hold a small legal ceremony in Australia with an authorised celebrant, and the NOIM applies exactly as above.
journey.reaction: Didn't know you could do the legal bit small in Australia and then party somewhere else. That's actually an idea for us.

journey.section: NOIM or marrying abroad: which paperwork applies?
journey.quote: DFAT can issue a CNI in Australia, but some local authorities accept only CNIs issued in their own country.
journey.reaction: Option B is a lot of detail for someone who came for the NOIM. I scrolled past most of it.

journey.quote: Can we lodge a NOIM if we live overseas?
journey.reaction: FAQ questions are the exact things I'd type into Google. Short answers, mostly repeating above, which is fine for skimmers.

journey.quote: How long does a Notice of Intended Marriage last?
journey.reaction: I read this as 'does it expire?'. The answer gives the window again, which I think means it's good for up to 18 months, but it doesn't quite say it in those words.

unanswered_questions: Who, in plain words, can witness a NOIM in Singapore? (The page points me to the form rather than naming them.)
Does a NOIM expire if our date moves past 18 months, or do we redo it?
Do you work with couples who live outside Australia?

turn_offs_found.quote: The authorised witnesses are listed in the "Signatures of parties and witnesses" section of the NOIM.
turn_offs_found.why: The heading asks 'Who can witness a Notice of Intended Marriage?' and the first line sends me to a PDF instead of answering. On a phone that's the moment I'd leave for another result that lists them.

turn_offs_found.quote: Destination couples either marry legally in Australia and celebrate abroad, which needs a NOIM, or marry legally abroad under local rules, often with a Certificate of No Impediment.
turn_offs_found.why: Takeaways are what I read first, and this one packs two routes plus a new acronym-to-be into one sentence. Took two reads on a small screen.

would_share_with: My fiance, for the overseas witnessing rule and the one month to 18 month window
A friend marrying in Sydney next year, for the timing section

cta_reaction.why: I came for a form, not a planner, and we're marrying at home in Australia, not abroad. The links weren't pushy and there were no pop-ups, so it didn't annoy me. If we did the 'legal at home, party abroad' idea, I'd come back. For now, bookmark.

top_3_changes: Under 'Who can witness a Notice of Intended Marriage?', open with a plain one-line answer naming the main types of authorised witness (from the form), then point to the form for the full list, so the heading's question is answered first.
Split the fourth Key takeaway into two short bullets (marry legally in Australia: NOIM; marry legally abroad: local rules), leaving the CNI detail to the body.

In the FAQ 'How long does a Notice of Intended Marriage last?', say directly whether the NOIM stays valid for up to 18 months and what happens if the date moves outside that window, to match how people read 'how long does it last'.

Stayed in character as Priya, a casual Google searcher on a phone

Journey types limited to gained_trust, lost_trust, confused, bored, excited, objection
